sources.name: Wikidata — explicitly attested country names
sources.licenseName: CC0 1.0 (structured name and country facts only)
sources.attribution: Wikidata contributors (2026), CC0 structured facts. Only explicit given/family-name entities, citizenship, documented birthplace or residence, and observed sex/gender facts. Includes expatriate/historical residents, not just citizens. No name-based nationality prediction, no inferred popularity ranks.

sources.name: World Gender-Name Dictionary 2.0 — country-specific original
sources.attribution: Raffo, Julio (2021), WGND 2.0, Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/MSEGSJ. Original name-gender-code only; no language-expanded associations, no weight-to-rank conversion. Country/gender classifications are reproduced from WGND, not independently inferred by NAMAE.

sources.name: Wikidata — observed people/name counts (not population ranks)
sources.attribution: Wikidata contributors (2026), CC0 structured facts. Explicit human, given/family name, observed gender and citizenship/birthplace/residence facts. Count DISTINCT person IDs after spelling normalization. Biased public-person corpus, not a census; no equivalent national-rank claim. Ties use competition ranks.

sources.name: WGND 1.0 — Country-specific names
sources.attribution: Raffo, Julio; Lax-Martinez, Gema (2018), WGND 1.0, doi:10.7910/DVN/YPRQH8. Country-specific original; no language expansion. Adapted by NAMAE.

sources.name: Record Atlas surname corpus
sources.attribution: Record Atlas surname corpus (2026). Names and attested countries only. Excludes phonetic guesses, counts and Wiktionary content. Adapted by NAMAE.

sources.licenseName: Supreme Court public material policy / published statistical facts
sources.attribution: 출처: 대한민국 대법원 전자가족관계등록시스템, 상위 출생신고 이름 현황, 2024년 시도별 여성 이름. NAMAE uses the published spellings as evidence of use. No regional count is displayed as a national count.

sources.name: KOSIS — 2015 census surname totals
sources.attribution: Source: KOSIS, Population and Housing Census 2015, DT_1IN15SD. NAMAE groups national surname totals by Hangul and retains the published Hanja as aliases.

sources.name: South Australia — Popular Baby Names
sources.attribution: Source: South Australian Attorney-General’s Department, Popular Baby Names. NAMAE aggregates the published counts for South Australian birth registrations 1944–2013 and converts display capitalization.

sources.name: National Records of Scotland — Babies’ First Names
sources.attribution: Contains public sector information from National Records of Scotland licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Published counts from Scottish birth registrations 1974–2025 are aggregated for UK name coverage.

sources.name: New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs — Baby Name Popularity Over Time
sources.attribution: Source: New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs, Baby Name Popularity Over Time, via Figure.NZ, CC BY 4.0. NAMAE sums registered birth counts across 1900–2025 and retains spellings with at least 20 registrations. Damaged source encodings and unusable labels are omitted. Counts are not current national prevalence.

sources.name: Central Statistics Office — Irish Babies’ Names
sources.attribution: Source: Central Statistics Office, Ireland. NAMAE aggregates published annual counts from VSA50 and VSA60 (1964–2025) and VSA110 (2023–2025). Suppressed counts are omitted.

sources.name: Thai Names Corpus — Korkeat Wannapat and contributors
sources.attribution: Thai Names Corpus by Korkeat Wannapat and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0. NAMAE filters spellings, deduplicates and orders the entries with other source data. The adapted entries identified by this source are also CC BY-SA 4.0. The source documents usage but gives no national frequency.

sources.name: BerlinOnline / LABO — Berlin birth registrations
sources.attribution: BerlinOnline GmbH, auf Basis von Daten des Berliner Landesamtes für Bürger- und Ordnungsangelegenheiten (LABO), https://github.com/berlin/haeufige-vornamen-berlin. NAMAE aggregates 2012–2023 counts and selects first-position names where position is published.

sources.name: Statistics Sweden — newborn given names 1998–2022
sources.attribution: NAMAE adaptation of Statistics Sweden's TAB5665. Annual counts are combined and suppressed cells are omitted.

sources.name: Swiss Federal Statistical Office — resident first names, 2025
sources.attribution: Source: Swiss Federal Statistical Office, STATPOP, 2025. NAMAE sums counts across birth cohorts and retains names with at least five residents in the published data.

sources.name: Israel CBS / Aviezer Lifshitz — babynamesIL
sources.attribution: Birth-name totals from Israel Central Bureau of Statistics, prepared by Aviezer Lifshitz (babynamesIL). NAMAE combines the published sectors for each name and sex.

sources.name: Chinese Gender — counts of given names in shareholder records
sources.attribution: Dongbo Shi and Sherry Tong Tong, Chinese Gender, Harvard Dataverse, DOI 10.7910/DVN/UAARYY. The aggregate sample covers shareholders in Chinese company records through 2018. The sampled counts describe this population. NAMAE retains up to 25,000 one- or two-character Han spellings per sex with at least 30 observations, excluding administrative labels.

sources.name: Naampy — counts of given names in historical Indian electoral rolls
sources.attribution: Gaurav Sood et al., naampy, Harvard Dataverse, DOI 10.7910/DVN/WZGJBM. NAMAE aggregates retained native-script spellings across the source's published state and birth-year groups. It requires at least 50 records for the recorded sex, at least 90% of the retained female and male counts, and at least five records in three separately reported groups. Counts reflect the historical electoral-roll sample.
